results.fact: Rappel anchor on Peak 1 vs 'no established rappel route'
results.correct_value: Descent is mostly down-climbing, but parties commonly make a short rappel from existing anchors at one or two steep steps (Peak 1's slabby crux; a step on the way to the high point that a class 3 gully can bypass).
results.evidence: A 2021 NWHikers trip report describes reaching 'the spot where everyone rappels' on the way to the main summit and a small gully that bypasses it. A separate 2025 trip report (different party) found an existing rappel station above Peak 1's slabby crux and rappelled it on descent, and also mentions the rappel below the high point with a class 3 gully bypass. Both independently contradict 'no established rappel route / no fixed rappel infrastructure'.

results.evidence: Retry searched for any account of a rappel off The Pyramid: the only rappel found in Southern Pickets reports is Degenhardt's single-rope rappel back to the start of its climb, and Inspiration's west-side rappels; the 2019 Pickets report mentions only low 5th moves leaving the ridge onto Pyramid, no rappel. Stephabegg and CascadeClimbers 2025 Pyramid report were blocked. The row's rappel mentions may conflate Degenhardt's rappel. Would settle it: a readable Pyramid West Ridge descent description (e.g. the 2025 CascadeClimbers TR).

An NPS ranger report for Crescent Creek Basin/Degenhardt notes firm snow needing crampons for an early start from the saddle down into Crescent Creek Basin (snow, not a roped glacier). The 2019 report crossed sagging snow bridges on a broken glacier; a 2020 solo report bypassed the small glacier on rock. Sources agree snow/crampons are seasonal but not on whether roped glacier kit is required. Would settle it: a CascadeClimbers TR (blocked here) or ranger note stating whether parties rope up for the Barrier crossing to Pyramid.

No new source with a gain figure to Terror Basin was readable (Stephabegg and CascadeClimbers blocked; the NPS ranger report gives no figure). Prior pass found a GPS track at about 5,835 ft cumulative to Terror Basin and another report near 4,000 ft, and reaching Crescent Creek Basin via the 6,200 ft notch adds more, so '6,000+' is not clearly wrong. Would settle it: two cumulative-gain figures for Goodell Creek to Terror Basin camp.
